<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, `packages/qa/scenarios/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf3e71f6210aeb43acb90879ff8e4ad3cfb31c51` — the merge of head `b71ea1c14fd74e1989d7e8d030f45c42c89e8e6b` into base `7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf3e71f6210aeb43acb90879ff8e4ad3cfb31c51 && git checkout cf3e71f6210aeb43acb90879ff8e4ad3cfb31c51
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 b71ea1c14fd74e1989d7e8d030f45c42c89e8e6b && git checkout -B drift-repro 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 && git merge --no-ff b71ea1c14fd74e1989d7e8d030f45c42c89e8e6b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b71ea1c14fd74e1989d7e8d030f45c42c89e8e6b`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the PR body is true and complete against the diff. New on `./runner`: `rollupSourceCharges`, `readRollupSourceFinding`, `RollupSourceCharge`, `RollupSourceReading` (`orchestrate.ts`), `rollupSourceFindings`, `rollupSourceChecks` (`scorecard.ts`), and the optional field `BuildHalf.rollupSourceUnreadable`. A new runtime dependency on `@objectstack/lint` (workspace, published, same version line); the lockfile entry and the test alias to the lint source follow from it and are stated in the body.

The answer that moves is declared. On a build whose artifact carries a standing `security-rollup-source-unreadable` finding on a card persona's own set, where that persona's `hidden` withholds the roll-up's child object or a child field the finding names, each finding is one failed Build check (in `total`, never in `passed`), a named Build finding, and a failing `rollup-source-unreadable:<persona>:<parent.field>` check in the record's `build` / `iterate-build` evidence. `buildPassed` refuses such a build, so template and ask modes no longer install it as the verified build. The rule runs on the built artifact through `validateRollupSourceVisibility`, never on the bounded `os build` tail, and reads only `objects`, `objectExtensions` and `permissions` via `resolveStackCollection`: deterministic, no model or network (cloud#3600). A finding the runner cannot read is not silently uncharged: `readRollupSourceFinding` throws and the half records `rollup-source: …` as its error, and the suite runs the real rule on every arm so a change of wording fails tests first. A set no persona holds, a child the card lets the persona read and the rule's `info` row-scope arm are not charged (pinned). Ask mode authors nothing and is never charged. A build with no such finding scores, renders and records as before (pinned). Measured on eval#1's live records: `project_with_tasks` 9 of 28 scratch builds charged, invoice 1 of 28, crm 0; 4 pass verdicts flip. The card's "15 of 15" was measured on the authoring transcripts; the finished build still carries the finding in 4 of those 15, which the PR states.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no spec key, app metadata, card JSON or lint rule changes. The widening is additive exports, one optional field and one workspace dependency of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`. The Build score moving on matching builds is the card's purpose and is declared.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no `packages/lint/**` change, no governed path, no platform runtime or security behaviour. `src/score/**` is untouched; the charge is added in the runner's tally beside `requiredCycles`, as the order allowed.
